description: Makes ONE copy of the input soundfile - CDP's own cp, verified BIT-IDENTICAL: decoded-sample sha256 equal to the source on both mono and stereo probes, duration static and sample-exact. No parameters at all. Submode 1 pinned; submode 2 (COPY MANY) is engine-dropped: it takes a COUNT instead of an outfile and self-names its outputs '<stem>_001.wav'... in the cwd (verified n1.wav -> n1_001/002/003.wav, exit 0, no argv output) - reach it via execute() with cwd control.
musical_use: The provenance anchor: materialise a session-owned copy of a source before destructive experiments, fork one lineage into two named branches that later diverge (copy first, then process each), or duplicate a reference render for A/B work where both files must live side by side. Since the copy is bit-identical (verified), it is safe anywhere in a bit-faithful chain - unlike re-encoding routes. Within this engine most duplication needs are covered by caching and lineage, but an explicit copy gives you a stable, user-visible file that later graph edits cannot invalidate.

examples.description: Snapshot a source before a destructive experiment.
examples.expected_use: Output is a bit-identical duplicate (verified equal decoded sha256); duration unchanged.

known_issues: No parameters; nothing to range-check. Output verified bit-identical to the input (mono and stereo).

Submode 2 (COPY MANY) has NO outfile argv - 'housekeep copy 2 infile count [-i]' self-names '<stem>_001.wav'..'<stem>_00N.wav' in the cwd (verified) and halts on pre-existing duplicates unless -i is set. Engine-incompatible; execute() with cwd control if needed.
